exercise.name: Bridge Mountain Climber (Cross Body)

reference.title: Bridge Mountain Climber (Cross Body)
reference.listing: Video (movement reference; the page could not be read at authoring time: gymvisual.com is blocked by the proxy, so the movement comes from the name and standard coaching practice)
reference.note: Reference used only to identify the movement. No GymVisual media is stored here; this rig, model and animation are original.

exercise.mechanics: Compound (single-leg hip extension held; opposite hip flexion with trunk rotation)

breathing.pattern: Breathe out as the hips rise and as each knee drives across, breathe in as the leg returns and as you lower.
breathing.cadence: About 1.5 s up, about 1.9 s per side, 2 s down

prescription.tempo: Knee in about 0.8 s, short pause, back in 0.8 s; hips stay up
prescription.progression: More knee drives per bridge, then a slow 2 s return, then a single-leg bridge hold.

cues.text: Lie on your back, knees bent, feet flat and hip width, arms on the floor by your sides.
Breathe out and push through the heels to lift the hips until knees, hips and shoulders line up.
Keep the hips high and level; drive the right knee toward the chest and across while the left elbow reaches toward it.
Return the foot and arm, then drive the left knee across toward the right elbow.
Breathe in and roll the hips down slowly.

mistakes.mistake: Hips dropping or tilting when a foot lifts
mistakes.fix: Press hard through the planted heel and squeeze that glute; keep the pelvis level.

mistakes.mistake: Twisting from the hips instead of the upper trunk
mistakes.fix: Keep the pelvis square; only the upper back turns a little.

mistakes.mistake: Yanking the head and neck forward
mistakes.fix: Reach with the elbow and keep the head heavy on the mat.
Move each leg under control, about a second each way.

kinematics.norm: Support hip extended to neutral in the bridge (Lehecka 2017)

kinematics.peak: Driving hip ≈92° flexion, 14° across the midline, knee ≈112°
kinematics.norm: Driving knee toward the chest and across the midline (clinical opinion)

kinematics.peak: Opposite elbow 34 cm from the knee; upper trunk turned ≈8°
kinematics.norm: Opposite elbow toward the knee with a small upper-trunk rotation; rotation-plus-flexion drills bring in the obliques (Escamilla 2006)

kinematics.setup: Hip joint 8.6 cm above the floor
kinematics.peak: 29.5 cm in the bridge, lowest 29.5 cm during the knee drives
kinematics.norm: Held level while one foot is up; single-leg bridging raised gluteal and hamstring demand (Lehecka 2017)

kinematics.peak: 1.5 s up, about 1.9 s per side, 2.0 s down, 0.9 s reset
kinematics.norm: Controlled, about 1 s each way (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual #22561, Bridge Mountain Climber (Cross Body), video (movement reference)
Lehecka et al. 2017, building a better gluteal bridge: EMG of hip muscles during modified single-leg bridges (Int J Sports Phys Ther 12(4):543-549; PMC5534144)
Macadam and Feser 2019, gluteus maximus EMG excitation during dynamic body-weight hip extension: a systematic review (Int J Sports Phys Ther 14(1):14-31; PMC6350668)
Escamilla et al. 2006, electromyographic analysis of traditional and nontraditional abdominal exercises: implications for rehabilitation and training (Phys Ther 86(5):656-671; PubMed 16649890)

cautions: Stop if sharp pain, numbness or giving-way occurs.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
Low-back discomfort at the top usually means arching: lift a little less and tuck the pelvis.
Hamstring cramping on the support leg: move the feet a little closer to the hips.
modify: Hard to keep the hips up: lift the knee straight up (no cross-body reach).
Neck tension: keep both arms on the floor.
regressions: Bridge march (knee straight up, arms down).

muscleNotes.glute_max_r: Holds the hips up on the planted side; single-leg bridging loads it more (Lehecka 2017).
muscleNotes.glute_max_l: Holds the hips up on the planted side; single-leg bridging loads it more (Lehecka 2017).
muscleNotes.obliques_r: Turn the upper trunk so the elbow reaches across (Escamilla 2006).
muscleNotes.obliques_l: Turn the upper trunk so the elbow reaches across (Escamilla 2006).
muscleNotes.hamstrings_r: Assist hip extension on the planted leg (Lehecka 2017).
muscleNotes.hamstrings_l: Assist hip extension on the planted leg (Lehecka 2017).
muscleNotes.hip_flexors_r: Drive the knee toward the chest (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.hip_flexors_l: Drive the knee toward the chest (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.core: Rectus abdominis keeps the ribs down and helps the reach (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.glute_med_r: Keeps the pelvis level on one leg (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.glute_med_l: Keeps the pelvis level on one leg (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_r: Hold the trunk line in the bridge (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_l: Hold the trunk line in the bridge (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.adductors_r: Bring the driving knee across the midline (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.adductors_l: Bring the driving knee across the midline (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_r: Lifts the reaching arm off the mat (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_l: Lifts the reaching arm off the mat (clinical opinion).
